column1: Stay with me.
Around minute eight, I'll take you to a fight India is in right now — in Andhra Pradesh.
And I'll give you the date that could decide how it ends.
First, let's give India its due.
Because that pharmacy of the world title?
India earned it.
Think back to two thousand one.
H.I.V. is killing millions in Africa.
The medicines exist... but the Western price is around ten thousand dollars a year for one patient.
Then an Indian company, Cipla, stands up and offers the same three-drug mix for about a dollar a day.
One dollar.
That one offer helped change how the world priced these medicines.
And today, you'll find India sells medicines abroad worth more than two and a half lakh crore rupees a year.
So where's the missing piece?
Here's the catch.
Every tablet has two parts.
There's the powder that actually makes you better.
The industry calls it the A.P.I. — and no, not the computer kind.
Let's just call it the powder.
And then there's everything around it... the rest of the tablet, the coating, the strip, the box.
And you should be proud of this.
Indian companies are world class at that last part.
Mixing, pressing, packing, and passing the toughest inspections on the planet.
But the powder you swallow?
A lot of it is made somewhere else first.
In twenty twenty-five, India bought these powders from other countries worth around sixty-five thousand crore rupees.
And the biggest seller, by far...
China.
